repos.name: kasike.dev
repos.what: This site. Static pages plus one small function, no framework.
repos.score: More than 150 automated checks pass on this build, including 12 failure-injection tests, with 0 accessibility violations.
repos.tradeoff: No framework and no build step on the host. I hand-rolled the routing and gave up convenience. In return an article page stays under 200 KB and the security policy stays strict.
repos.fix: Article pages were downloading the whole 3D scene. It now loads only on the tower page: 2.4 MB down to 174 KB.

commits.text: Article pages were downloading the whole 3D scene. It now loads only on the tower page: 2.4 MB down to 174 KB.
First production build of this site: real page addresses, self-hosted fonts and strict security headers.

repos.name: Aurevon Ventures
repos.what: Company site with memberships, Stripe payments and automatic Discord access.
repos.score: Public copy cut by 37%: 58.5k characters down to 37k across 21 pages.
repos.tradeoff: A subscriber is identified from the Stripe customer record, not from an email typed into a request. More plumbing, but a request cannot claim someone else’s subscription.
repos.fix: Payment methods that settle later were reported as complete before the money arrived. Fulfilment now waits for the funds.

commits.text: Buy-one-get-one orders no longer earn a membership pass, and a duplicate product listing is gone. The site copy and the back end now agree.
Cut the public pages down to headings, facts and actions: 58.5k characters of text to 37k across 21 pages.
Wrote down the verified production setup and the rules for payments, intake and Discord, so every later change follows them.
Payment lifecycle tightened: nothing ships before funds settle, and a cancelled member loses access cleanly.
A payment lookup was failing in production with no reason recorded. Added the logging needed to find the cause.

repos.name: Forge
repos.what: A custom storefront with Shopify behind the counter, and a shopping assistant in the chat.
repos.score: Every push runs unit tests, lint and a smoke test against production after it deploys.
repos.tradeoff: The chat assistant runs under a hard spending cap with strict request checks. It refuses before it overspends.
repos.fix: Adding an item from the chat covered the conversation with the cart, so a shopper could not keep talking. Fixed in the next push.

commits.text: Hardened the chat’s rate limit so a visitor cannot dodge it.
Adding an item from the chat used to cover the conversation with the cart. Now you can keep talking.
The post-deploy check now waits until production is serving the new code, then smoke-tests it.
Ask Forge chat: requests are validated, spend is capped, cart options are strict and the widget is accessible.
Automated checks now cover the storefront, the post-deploy check actually runs, and lint errors block a merge.

repos.name: Interlude
repos.what: A marketplace for AI wait time: sponsors pay for verified seconds, the person waiting earns a share.
repos.score: Billing audit: an exact 25.000000% split across 31 settled sessions, zero ledger drift, and settle-once held under 25 parallel requests.
repos.tradeoff: Backups upload off-site from inside the app, because the production image ships without a storage client. One more thing to maintain, nothing extra to install on the server.
repos.fix: A stress audit turned up ten findings and a real phone turned up three layout bugs. All thirteen are closed.

commits.text: Took the site public: removed the preview password gate and the code that only existed to support it.
Documented two settings that scripts read but the setup checklist never mentioned.
Tested on a real phone screen, found three wallet layout bugs (one tab was cut off) and fixed them.
Built off-site backups into the app, because the production server had no tool to upload them.
Closed all ten findings from an end-to-end stress audit. The billing core itself came out exact.

repos.name: Aurevon Labs
repos.what: The Labs site and the media pipeline behind the scheduled @AurevonLabs posts.
repos.score: 28 of 28 images passed verification (size, checksum, format) before they went live.
repos.tradeoff: Post images ship as plain files on the site instead of through an upload service. Every pack is a commit: slower to publish, fully traceable.
repos.fix: A generated graphic went out with garbled labels. Rebuilt it with letter-perfect copy.

commits.text: Added the September 29 image pack so the scheduler can pull it from the Labs site.
A generated graphic shipped with garbled labels. Rebuilt it with letter-perfect copy.

Added 28 article images. Each file was verified by size, checksum and format before it went live.
